title: Running a compiler from an editor
hints: Parse the location first and the rest second. For MSVC the location is `file(` up to `): `; for Clang it is `file:line:col: `. Skip the first two characters when looking for the location's separator if the line starts with a drive letter like `C:`.
For `collect`, split each stream separately (reuse your line collector from lesson 1.04), then run every line through `parseDiagnostic`.
requirements: Both diagnostic styles are parsed, including drive letters, missing columns and missing codes.
Each stream's chunks are joined into lines independently, with Windows line endings handled.
Errors and warnings are counted, and the status reflects crashes, errors and plain failures.
stretch: Run a real compiler: start `cl.exe` (from a Developer Command Prompt environment) on a small file with an error, capturing stdout and stderr on two threads as lesson 1.04 describes, and feed the captured chunks to `collect`.
